sections.h2: China supplies 38.8% of India's lock imports, and its share is still rising

chart.title: China alone accounts for 38.8%; no other supplier reaches 15%
chart.sub: Share of India's FY2024-25 imports under HS 8301, %.
chart.source: DGCI&S EIDB, Commodity x Country-wise report.

sections.means: China's 38.8% share of India's lock imports is the largest single-supplier position in the trade data.
sections.todo: Track China's share in each year's HS 8301 data before linking it to Dindigul, since the post finds no measured effect on the cluster.

sections.h2: India's lock imports rose 5.79% to US$197.84 million in FY2024-25

chart.title: Lock imports grew in FY2024-25 but remain a small slice of the import bill
chart.sub: Import value under HS 8301, US$ million.

sections.means: Imports under this HS code are growing, yet the post puts them at a small share of India's US$721.2-billion import bill.
sections.todo: Re-check the HS 8301 total in the next DGCI&S release so the growth rate is tested against a third year.

sections.h2: Dindigul's manufacturer count fell from about 2,000 to about 60, by one count

chart.title: Trade-press counts show a steep fall, though other sources disagree on the base
chart.sub: Manufacturers in the Dindigul cluster, as cited in DT Next reporting.

sections.means: The steep fall rests on one trade-press count, and the GI filing's 3,125 manufacturers and the 43-unit directory count cannot be reconciled with it.
sections.todo: Commission one agreed census of active Dindigul units before judging the GI premium or GST carve-out plans, since no official count exists.
